title: CODE-SHARP: Continuous Open-ended Discovery and Evolution of Skills as Hierarchical Reward Programs
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Two coupled foundation-model loops, one proposing and one mutating, jointly grow a shared archive of reusable skills with feedback from failures.
layout: Central archive graph flanked by two vertical pipelines, with feedback loops along the bottom
description: A wide diagram with a large boxed graph labeled 'Skill Archive' at the center. The graph is a dense network of green and yellow nodes (squares, circles, diamonds) joined by gray edges. Two vertical stacks of modules sit on either side. On the left, in purple shades, are the Skill Proposal Generator, Implementor and Judge, then a Syntax Check with a code-refinement loop, and finally an environment globe labeled RL Training. On the right, in light blue, are the Skill Mutation Generator and Implementor, a Syntax Check, and an environment-evaluation globe. Robot icons mark the foundation-model steps. Inputs run along the top: Failed Proposals, Skill Type, Environment Code, Mutation Type and Failed Mutations. Yellow and orange arrows carry the environment code and the sampled parent skill into the generators. Green arrows return accepted skills and mutations to the archive. Red dashed arrows send failures back to the inputs.
caption: \Name{} consists of two FM-driven iterative processes that discover and evolve skill encoding SHARPs. The skill proposal generator, implementor, and judge generate and filter novel SHARPs before environment evaluation. The skill mutation generator and implementor produce mutated versions of existing SHARPs, evaluated directly in the environment.
abstract: A core quality of general intelligence is the ability to open-endedly expand and evolve its set of mastered skills autonomously. While recent Foundation Model (FM) driven approaches have shown promising results towards this goal, they typically rely on significant human-in-the-loop engineering, limiting their transferability to novel environments. To address this, we introduce Continuous Open-ended Discovery and Evolution of Skills as Hierarchical Reward Programs (CODE-SHARP), a framework that leverages FMs to open-endedly grow and evolve an archive of Python programs encoding skills to train a generalist agent policy entirely from scratch via reinforcement learning, directly from source code. These programs, termed Skills as Hierarchical Reward Programs (SHARPs), each encode a local success condition and a set of prerequisites delegated to previously discovered SHARPs. At runtime, SHARPs dynamically route the agent through their prerequisite chain based on the current state, rewarding each completion along the way, requiring the agent to learn only the marginal behaviour each new SHARP introduces, enabling efficient learning of long-horizon skills without any pre-defined rewards. On Craftax-Classic and XLand-MiniGrid, agents trained fully autonomously by CODE-SHARP outperform previous works by 6x and 2.7x in median performance and are the only agents capable of crafting iron tools and mining diamonds. On AI2-THOR, CODE-SHARP achieves 66.7% median success versus 0% for ELLM and OMNI, using only the initial environment state instead of the full source code. Scaled to Craftax-Extended, CODE-SHARP trains a generalist agent on over 90 discovered SHARPs, enabling the agent to solve challenging long-horizon tasks zero-shot, matching agents trained on ground-truth rewards.
